questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Lenz's law and conservation of energy
questions.question: A bar magnet is rapidly pulled away from a stationary conducting circular loop. The South pole of the magnet is the end facing the loop. If an observer looks at the loop from the side of the retreating magnet, what is the direction of the induced current in the loop?
questions.explanation: According to Lenz's law, the induced current must oppose the change producing it. The South pole is moving away, reducing the magnetic flux. To oppose this, the loop must attract the retreating South pole by acting as a magnetic North pole. By the Right-Hand Grip Rule, a magnetic North pole pointing toward the observer corresponds to a counter-clockwise current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the correct dimensional formula for Magnetic Flux (Φ_B)?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ_B = B · A. From the Lorentz force F = qvB, we have B = F / (qv). Dimensions of F = [MLT⁻²], q =[AT], v = [LT⁻¹]. Thus B = [MT⁻²A⁻¹]. Area A = [L²]. Multiplying them gives Φ_B = [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A closely wound coil has 100 turns. The magnetic flux passing through each turn of the coil changes uniformly from 0.5 Wb to 0.1 Wb in exactly 0.2 seconds. What is the magnitude of the average induced electromotive force (EMF) in the entire coil?
questions.explanation: Faraday's Law states E = -N (ΔΦ/Δt). Here N = 100, ΔΦ = 0.1 - 0.5 = -0.4 Wb, and Δt = 0.2 s. Magnitude |E| = 100 × (0.4 / 0.2) = 100 × 2 = 200 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a standard operating AC generator, what is the phase difference between the time-varying magnetic flux linked with the armature coil and the alternating EMF induced in it?
questions.explanation: The magnetic flux linked with the coil is Φ(t) = NAB cos(ωt). The induced EMF is the negative derivative of the flux: E(t) = -dΦ/dt = NABω sin(ωt). A sine wave and a cosine wave are perfectly out of phase by exactly 90° (or π/2 radians).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car is traveling horizontally due East at a high speed. It has a perfectly straight, vertical radio antenna. Assume the Earth's magnetic field in this localized region is completely horizontal and points perfectly due North. Which end of the vertical antenna is at a higher electrical potential due to motional EMF?
options: Both ends are at the same potential
questions.explanation: The velocity vector v points East. The magnetic field B points North. The magnetic Lorentz force on a positive charge is F_q = q(v × B). Applying the Right-Hand Rule: Point fingers East, curl them North. The thumb points Up. Therefore, positive charges are pushed to the top end of the antenna, making the top end physically at a higher electrical potential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The steady current in an inductive coil decreases uniformly from 5 A to 2 A in exactly 0.1 seconds. If the average induced EMF in the coil during this time is 60 V, what is the self-inductance of the coil?
questions.explanation: The formula for induced EMF in an inductor is |E| = L (|ΔI| / Δt). Given |E| = 60 V, |ΔI| = 5 - 2 = 3 A, and Δt = 0.1 s. Solving for L: 60 = L * (3 / 0.1) = L * 30. Therefore, L = 60 / 30 = 2.0 H.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Lenz's law and conservation of energy
questions.question: Two identical, long, vertical hollow pipes are set up; one is made of solid pure copper and the other of PVC (insulating plastic). Two identical strong neodymium bar magnets are dropped simultaneously from rest down the exact centers of each pipe. Which of the following statements perfectly describes their descent?
options: Both magnets hit the ground at exactly the same time.
The magnet in the copper pipe hits the ground first.
The magnet in the PVC pipe hits the ground first.
The magnet in the copper pipe stops completely and hovers inside.
questions.explanation: The copper pipe is a conductor. The falling magnet induces eddy currents in the walls of the pipe. By Lenz's law, these eddy currents create magnetic fields that strongly oppose the magnet's motion, slowing its fall. The PVC pipe is an insulator, so no eddy currents form, and the magnet falls freely under gravity. Thus, the magnet in the PVC pipe hits the ground first.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A standard horizontal U-shaped conducting frame is placed in a uniform vertical magnetic field B. A straight conducting rod of length L and resistance R rests on the parallel arms of the frame and is pulled mechanically to the right with a constant velocity v. Assuming the frame itself has negligible resistance, what is the exact mechanical power that the external agent must continually supply to maintain this constant velocity?
questions.explanation: Motional EMF E = B L v. Induced current I = E/R = (B L v)/R. The magnetic drag force opposing the pull is F_m = I L B = (B L v / R) L B = (B² L² v) / R. To maintain constant velocity, the external force F_ext must equal F_m. Mechanical power P = F_ext * v = [(B² L² v) / R] * v = (B² L² v²) / R.
questions.imagePrompt: A top-down schematic of a horizontal U-shaped metallic frame. A straight metallic rod of length L sits across the open parallel arms. A uniform magnetic field (indicated by X marks) points into the page. A force vector 'F' is pulling the rod to the right at a constant velocity 'v'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two incredibly long, ideal coaxial solenoids are constructed. The inner solenoid has radius r₁ and n₁ turns per unit length. The outer solenoid has radius r₂ (where r₂ > r₁) and n₂ turns per unit length. What is the mutual inductance per unit length of this coaxial system?
questions.explanation: To find mutual inductance M, pass a current I through the outer solenoid. The magnetic field inside it is uniform: B₂ = μ₀ n₂ I. This field passes through the inner solenoid. The flux linked with one turn of the inner solenoid is Φ_turn = B₂ · A₁ = (μ₀ n₂ I) (π r₁²). For a length l, the inner solenoid has N₁ = n₁ l turns. Total flux Φ_total = (n₁ l) (μ₀ n₂ I π r₁²). Mutual inductance M = Φ_total / I = μ₀ π r₁² n₁ n₂ l. Mutual inductance per unit length M/l = μ₀ π r₁² n₁ n₂.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A circular wire loop of radius r is situated in a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicularly to the plane of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic field decays exponentially with time according to B(t) = B₀ e^(-αt), where B₀ and α are positive constants. What is the exact magnitude of the induced EMF in the loop at the very instant t = 0?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ(t) = B(t) · A = (B₀ e^(-αt)) (π r²). The magnitude of induced EMF is |E| = |dΦ/dt| = |π r² B₀ (-α e^(-αt))| = π r² B₀ α e^(-αt). At the exact instant t = 0, e⁰ = 1, so |E| = π r² B₀ α.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A graph plots the magnetic flux Φ passing through a closed loop on the y-axis against time t on the x-axis. The graph is shaped like an isosceles triangle: it starts at the origin (0,0), rises linearly to a sharp peak at time t₀, and then falls linearly back to zero at time 2t₀. Which of the following describes the resulting graph of the induced EMF (E) versus time t over the interval 0 to 2t₀?
options: A positive constant step followed immediately by a negative constant step of equal magnitude.
A negative constant step followed immediately by a positive constant step of equal magnitude.
A V-shaped pulse exactly mirroring the flux graph.
A horizontal straight line at a constant positive value.
questions.explanation: By Faraday's Law, E = -dΦ/dt. The EMF is the negative of the slope of the flux graph. From t = 0 to t₀, the flux increases linearly, so the slope (dΦ/dt) is a positive constant. Therefore, E is a negative constant. From t₀ to 2t₀, the flux decreases linearly back to zero, so the slope is a negative constant. Therefore, E is a positive constant. This results in a negative step pulse followed immediately by a positive step pulse.
questions.imagePrompt: A 2D line graph. The y-axis is Magnetic Flux (Φ) and the x-axis is time (t). A solid line traces an isosceles triangle, starting at (0,0), rising diagonally to a peak at x=t₀, and descending symmetrically back to the x-axis at x=2t₀.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
PASSAGE: An industrial AC generator consists of a flat rectangular coil of 500 turns. The coil has physical dimensions of 0.2 m × 0.1 m and a total internal electrical resistance of 10 Ω. It is forced to rotate mechanically at a constant speed of 3000 rpm within a uniform magnetic field of 0.05 T. The axis of rotation is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

What is the absolute peak (maximum) induced electromotive force generated by this coil?
questions.explanation: Peak EMF E₀ = N A B ω. Here N = 500, Area A = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 m², B = 0.05 T. Angular velocity ω = 3000 rpm = 3000 × (2π / 60) rad/s = 100π rad/s. E₀ = 500 × 0.02 × 0.05 × 100π = 10 × 0.05 × 100π = 0.5 × 100π = 50π V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: If the external terminals of the generator are temporarily short-circuited (external resistance is zero), what is the maximum mechanical torque that the driving engine must supply to maintain the 3000 rpm rotation?
questions.explanation: When short-circuited, the only resistance is internal: R = 10 Ω. The maximum current is I₀ = E₀ / R = 50π / 10 = 5π A. The magnetic torque opposing the rotation is τ = N I A B sin(ωt). Maximum torque occurs when sin(ωt) = 1 and current is at peak I₀. τ_max = N I₀ A B = 500 × (5π) × 0.02 × 0.05 = 500 × 0.001 × 5π = 0.5 × 5π = 2.5π N·m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: The rotation is stopped completely. The coil is positioned so that its plane is perfectly perpendicular to the magnetic field. It is then quickly yanked out of the magnetic field region entirely in a time span of 0.1 seconds. What is the average induced EMF during this rapid extraction?
questions.explanation: Average EMF E_avg = N (|ΔΦ| / Δt). Initial flux per turn Φ_i = B A = 0.05 × 0.02 = 0.001 Wb. Final flux Φ_f = 0. Thus |ΔΦ| = 0.001 Wb. E_avg = 500 × (0.001 / 0.1) = 500 × 0.01 = 5.0 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A highly sensitive circular coil of resistance 40 Ω, possessing 100 turns and a radius of 0.1 m, is placed perfectly perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. It is then rapidly pulled entirely out of the field. What is the total electrical charge that physically flows through the coil wire during this extraction process?
questions.explanation: The total charge flown is ΔQ = N |ΔΦ| / R. Area A = πr² = π(0.1)² = 0.01π m². Initial flux per turn Φ_i = BA = 0.5 × 0.01π = 0.005π Wb. Final flux Φ_f = 0, so |ΔΦ| = 0.005π. ΔQ = (100 × 0.005π) / 40 = 0.5π / 40 = π / 80 C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rigid square conducting loop of side a and resistance R is being pulled at a constant velocity v completely out of a region of uniform magnetic field B. The plane of the loop is perpendicular to the field, and its velocity vector is perpendicular to one of its edges. What is the total mechanical work done by the external pulling force to remove the loop completely from the field?
questions.explanation: The motional EMF induced while pulling the loop out is E = Bav. The induced current is I = E/R = Bav/R. The magnetic dragging force opposing the motion acts on the trailing edge: F_m = IaB = (Bav/R)aB = B²a²v/R. To pull the loop completely out, this constant force must be applied over a distance equal to the width of the loop, a. Total work W = F_m × distance = (B²a²v/R) × a = B²a³v / R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A straight conducting rod of mass m and length L slides frictionlessly down two parallel conducting rails. The rails are inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal. A uniform magnetic field B exists in the strictly **vertical** direction (pointing downwards). The rails are connected at the bottom by a resistor R. Neglecting the resistance of the rod and rails, what is the steady terminal velocity v_t achieved by the sliding rod?
questions.explanation: The horizontal component of the rod's velocity cuts the vertical B-field: v_x = v cosθ. Motional EMF E = B L v_x = B L v cosθ. Induced current I = (B L v cosθ) / R. The magnetic force on the rod is strictly horizontal: F_m = I L B = (B² L² v cosθ) / R. We balance the forces *along the incline*. The component of gravity pulling down the incline is F_g = mg sinθ. The component of the horizontal magnetic force pushing *up* the incline is F_{m,up} = F_m cosθ = (B² L² v cos²θ) / R. At terminal velocity v_t, these balance: mg sinθ = (B² L² v_t cos²θ) / R. Solving for v_t gives v_t = (mg R sinθ) / (B² L² cos²θ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A tiny circular wire loop of radius r is placed exactly at the geometric center of a much larger square wire loop of side length L (where r ≪ L). Both loops lie perfectly flat in the exact same plane. What is the mutual inductance M of this highly asymmetric two-loop system?
questions.explanation: Assume a current I flows in the large square loop. The distance from any side to the center is d = L/2. The magnetic field at the center from one side is B₁ = (μ₀I / 4πd) (sin 45° + sin 45°) = (μ₀I / 2πL) (2/√2) = μ₀I / (√2 π L). For 4 sides, total field B = 4 × B₁ = (2√2 μ₀ I) / (π L). Because the inner circle is very small, this field is essentially uniform over its area. Flux through small circle Φ = B · (πr²) = [(2√2 μ₀ I) / (π L)] πr² = (2√2 μ₀ r² I) / L. Mutual inductance M = Φ / I = (2√2 μ₀ r²) / L.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform but intensely time-varying magnetic field is confined to a perfectly cylindrical region of radius R. The magnetic field points into the page and its magnitude is increasing linearly with time as B(t) = α t (where α is a positive constant). What is the exact magnitude of the acceleration experienced by a stationary electron (charge e, mass m) placed at a radial distance r (where r > R) from the center of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: A time-varying magnetic field induces a non-conservative electric field. Use Faraday's Law in integral form: ∮ E · dl = -dΦ_B/dt. For r > R, choose a circular Amperian loop of radius r. ∮ E · dl = E(2πr). The magnetic flux Φ_B only exists within the radius R, so Φ_B = B(t) · πR² = (αt)πR². The derivative dΦ_B/dt = απR². Equating magnitudes: E(2πr) = απR² => E = (αR²) / (2r). The force on the electron is F = eE = (eαR²) / (2r). The acceleration a = F/m = (eαR²) / (2mr).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A specialized inductor is built in the shape of a toroid with a strictly rectangular cross-section. The inner radius of the toroid is a, the outer radius is b, and the vertical height of the rectangular cross-section is h. It is uniformly and tightly wound with a total of N turns of superconducting wire. What is the exact self-inductance L of this rectangular toroid?
questions.explanation: Apply Ampere's Law to find the magnetic field inside the toroid at a radial distance r (a < r < b): B(r) = (μ₀ N I) / (2π r). To find the total flux linked with the toroid, integrate the flux over the rectangular cross-section. A differential strip has height h and width dr. Flux through a single turn dΦ₁ = B(r) dA =[(μ₀ N I) / (2π r)] (h dr). Total flux for one turn Φ₁ = ∫_a^b[(μ₀ N I h) / (2π r)] dr = (μ₀ N I h / 2π) ln(b/a). Since there are N turns in series, total flux linkage Φ_total = N Φ₁ = (μ₀ N² I h / 2π) ln(b/a). Self-inductance L = Φ_total / I = (μ₀ N² h / 2π) ln(b/a).
questions.imagePrompt: A 3D schematic rendering of a section of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section. The inner radius is prominently labeled 'a', extending from the vertical central axis. The outer radius is labeled 'b'. The vertical height of the hollow rectangular tunnel inside is labeled 'h'. Wire wrappings are indicated looping around this rectangular profile.
